implementationNotes: MEASURED 2026-10-26 (plan lead329-ward-release accepted). (1) Linux ARM64 runner CAN cross-compile darwin-arm64: bun install --frozen-lockfile --os=darwin --cpu=arm64 pulls @napi-rs/keyring-darwin-arm64, then bun build --compile --target=bun-darwin-arm64 with the build.ts flags yields a 64271714-byte Mach-O arm64 executable that runs on the Mac and prints its version (scratch run 40366619824 on ward-cli#179, closed and branch deleted, never merged). Signature is adhoc,linker-signed, TeamIdentifier not set. codesign --verify reports invalid signature for every bun-compiled binary including the operator dist/ward, so that is baseline, not a cross-build defect. (2) Stability: the build is deterministic per OUTPUT FILE NAME. Same name gives identical bytes across directories and across hosts (runner ward-a sha256 1c3262ac... equals the Mac ward-a, cdhash d9c55540...); a different name gives different bytes and cdhash (ward-b2 90d70202, ward-c d6ee017b, ward-d d3f406cf, ward-e 2d3993f7 locally). So a release built as the fixed name ward from a fixed SHA is reproducible, and the designated requirement is the cdhash, which changes only when source or name changes. Not measured: that the keychain ACL honours the cdhash across a rebuild of the same bytes. (3) Synthetic cross-build, in-process, no keychain, scratch only: dev-era (origin/dev, snapshot 1) vault without approvals parses on the release tree; a dev-era approval gives vault_format_unsupported on the release tree; a release approval parses on release and is refused by the dev tree. The operator real ~/.ward was not opened.

---
A version-mismatched approval is ABSENT for authorisation, per record, as ADR 0018 already promises. Because DEC-246 D1 says "an authority record must never silently drop", it must also hold:
1. It authorises NOTHING, ever: no path reads a v1 record as approved. A test pins a literal v1 approval and asserts that it authorises nothing, and that the rest of the document still parses and works.
2. It stays VISIBLE: status (and doctor) name each stale approval, its checkout and its snapshot version, with the re-approve step.
3. It is never removed SILENTLY. Re-approving the same profile replaces it. Any other removal, including one bound to a deleted checkout, either keeps the record inert in the document or drops it with the drop named in that command's output. ward-cli picks either; a silent rewrite is not allowed.
4. Only a mismatched approval VERSION gets this treatment. An unknown key, a malformed record or a wrong document version still refuses the whole document, per D1.
ward-cli amends ADR 0018 and ADR 0010 to say this. One Opus re-review covers this delta together with the MEDIUM and LOW fixes you already dispatched. Rails unchanged: no tag, no main and no Release until it approves.
B is rejected: revoke and unregister reach only the current checkout, so a deleted worktree's approval would dead-end the operator sitting.
Your execution items (tag-time merge-base, gating publish on push, the reproducibility runbook step, the LOWs) are agreed.

The chosen arm for clause 3 is KEEP INERT: unregister and every other write carry the stale record through. ADR 0018 and ADR 0010 amended. The install runbook's re-approval step and Rollback section updated. new findings:

1. MEDIUM. status and doctor list stale approvals from the whole vault, not this checkout or project. reporting.ts:466-478 (staleApprovalReports), used at :409 and :556.
- Failure:
  - staleApprovalReports maps every state.staleProfileApprovals entry with no filter, including other projects' projectId, profile names and checkout paths.
  - That violates spec §8 (WARD_MVP_AGENT_SPEC.md:186, "no global inventory").
  - It violates ADR 0007:48-58 ("Only the current checkout… never enumerates the vault… that project is never named"), the module header at reporting.ts:10-13, and the command contract at manifest.ts:247 ("for the current project only").
  - status is admin:false, and SKILL.md:12 tells agents to run `ward status --json`, so this inventory lands in agent context.
  - ADR 0007's sentinel test seeds a second project and binding but no approval, so nothing catches it.
- Fix I'd accept:
  - Scope the named entries to the current project (manifest or binding projectId). That keeps the project's deleted-worktree records visible and names no other project.
  - Anything outside that scope is omitted, or reported as a bare count.
  - Add a sentinel test with a second-project stale approval, and amend ADR 0007.
  - (a2) clause 2 says "each stale approval", which collides with a recorded spec row. Route the scoping to opum-doc as an A/B; do not pick it in ward-cli. It interacts with finding 2: scoping to the current checkout would hide deleted worktrees and break clause 2; scoping to the current project would not.

2. MEDIUM. A stale record often cannot be cleared, so `ward doctor` fails on it permanently. reporting.ts:637-638, vault-state.ts:1103-1126, profiles.ts:473, :507-508, :589-593.
- Failure:
  - staleApprovalsCheck fails with reapprove_required whenever any stale record exists.
  - The only clearing write is re-approval matching profile, projectId, root, device and inode. That means:
    - a live directory with the same inode;
    - a live binding (writeApproval → requireBinding, :473);
    - the profile still declared in the manifest (:507-508).
  - Revoke looks only at active records (:589-593, profile_not_approved), and unregister reaches only the current binding.
  - So a stale record on a deleted worktree, a re-cloned directory, an unregistered checkout or an undeclared profile can never be cleared. The unregistered case is the very state unregister.test.ts deliberately leaves.
  - doctor then exits 6 in every checkout, permanently, and names a step that cannot be carried out. Install runbook step 8 cannot be completed.
  - A developer who just wants the stale record gone has to grant new authority and then revoke it.
  - This is the deleted-worktree dead end DEC-246 rejected B for. It is likely at the operator sitting, though I cannot see ~/.ward.
  - Keep-inert itself is allowed by clause 3. The defect is the permanent `fail` combined with an impossible remedy.
- Fix I'd accept, either:
  - (a) doctor fails only for a stale record whose checkout still resolves (same root, device and inode) and whose profile can still be approved. It names the others as inert and unreachable without failing, and the runbook says so.
  - (b) A terminal-only command that drops a named stale record and names the drop in its output (clause 3's second arm).
  - (b) is a new command, and (a) changes what doctor reports. Route the choice through opum-doc together with finding 1.
